scope: Visual evidence for ATS dining-room floor, lower walls, upper walls and ceiling. Research only; no UE or project edits.
method: Direct visual inspection of original-size local photographs, web search and source-page verification. No AI-generated or AI-upscaled evidence. Photographic colour is not a measured albedo.

observations: Warm beige terrazzo field containing dense irregular black, grey and light aggregate. Dark charcoal/black terrazzo bands contain contrasting pale aggregate.
Fine square slab joints are visible within the light terrazzo field. Dark strips form at least several orthogonal divisions in the visible portion.
Water, mud, exposure and artificial light affect the apparent golden colour and strong mirror reflection. These are not the normal dry finish.

Lower walls and column wraps have pale cream/grey/pink small rectangular mosaic units alternating direction in a basketweave or maze-like pattern, with a narrow dark tiled top border and dark skirting.

Upper walls, ceiling slab and substantial exposed downstand beams are painted off-white. Suspended linear light fittings, ceiling fans and exposed conduit are visible. No suspended square ceiling grid is visible in this room portion.
The rightmost wall also includes a large reflective panel surface. Its material, extent and relationship to the plan cannot be established.
limits: Cleanup furniture positions are not evidence of normal seating layout.
The source does not give dimensional plans or a camera position registered to the UE model.
This is the same photograph as a small image in the 2023 school newsletter, not independent corroboration.

observations: Group activity in a matching hall: tall windows, cross, blue wall fans, white beams and narrow suspended lights.

Foreground has dry-looking warm light beige terrazzo with small dark/light chips and a broad dark terrazzo band. It is substantially less golden and less mirror-reflective than the flood-cleanup image.
The right column clearly shows the pale rectangular alternating-direction mosaic and narrow dark cap border, independently corroborating that surface appearance before the 2023 flood.
Exposed white ceiling beams and fans agree with the 2023 image.
limits: People obscure much of the floor and furniture. No whole-room band map or measured tile scale can be recovered.
Matching room identification is a visual inference, not a labelled floorplan registration.
Image white balance has a green cast; do not sample it as exact material colour.

sources.publication_period: 2026/27 according to filename; photograph capture date unspecified
observations: Dining students use white rectangular tables and blue/aqua individual plastic chairs.
The visible lower wall is pale pink with a fine regular square-like grid, unlike the clearly alternating rectangular mosaic on the 2021/2023 hall columns.
A small patch of speckled grey/beige floor is visible at the right edge. No ceiling or top wall border is visible.
limits: The photo cannot establish that every dining wall is pink square mosaic or establish the wall's location in the user plan.
Do not assume a photo in a 2026/27 publication was captured in 2026 or supersedes all older images.
An unlabelled small timber door at the edge cannot override the user's confirmation of roller-shutter entrances.

observations: A washing/cleaning space with large windows, pale pink right lower wall, warmer beige left lower wall, off-white upper walls and dark skirting.
No narrow black top cap like the main hall column is clearly visible; the picture does not establish whether it is another section or a later alteration.
Students use red plastic basins on a long metal bench. The visible setup does not prove the location or design of the user's fixed long washbasin.
limits: Do not transfer this wall finish or the basin bench to an unverified position in the dining plan.

cross_photo_conclusions.floor: High confidence that the photographed main hall uses light warm beige speckled terrazzo with contrasting dark speckled bands. A generic near-monochrome grey floor is a poor match. Dry appearance should not copy the flood image's mud colour or wet gloss.
cross_photo_conclusions.lower_wall: High confidence in pale alternating-direction rectangular mosaic on the main hall columns and several walls in 2021/2023. Other dining/cleaning photos show pink fine-grid wall areas; exact zoning and age are unresolved. Neither uniform pink square tiles everywhere nor basketweave everywhere is established.
cross_photo_conclusions.upper_wall_ceiling: High confidence in off-white paint on exposed structural ceiling, beams, upper walls and columns in the photographed hall. A tiled drop-ceiling appearance has no support here. Exact beam, column and fixture coordinates remain unknown.

safe_appearance_changes: Use warm light beige terrazzo with small irregular multi-tone aggregate as the general photographed hall floor appearance.
Prepare a separate dark terrazzo material for photo-confirmed strips, but apply strips only after their world positions can be registered; do not generate a whole-room invented grid.
Use off-white low-gloss paint for the existing upper wall and ceiling geometry.

Prepare the pale rectangular alternating-direction mosaic and narrow dark cap for positively matched wall/column surfaces. Retain the pink-grid evidence as a separate unresolved zone instead of overwriting every wall.
Do not add a fabricated regular beam grid, ceiling tile grid, conduit network or identical light-spacing pattern.

shader_starting_points_not_site_measurem.notice: The following are renderer tuning suggestions only, not measured ATS material properties or calibrated colours. Verify under neutral illumination before adjusting the existing scene lighting.

dry_light_terrazzo.normal: Very shallow aggregate texture; avoid cobblestone relief or deep grout.
dry_light_terrazzo.colour: Low-saturation warm ivory/beige matrix, dark grey and light chips; avoid yellow flood-water tint.

dark_terrazzo.colour: Charcoal matrix with many light grey/white irregular chips.

pale_mosaic.colour: Off-white/light grey tiles with subtle cream or pink variation, restrained grout contrast.
pale_mosaic.normal: Small shallow joints; do not represent tiny mosaic as coarse 5 cm squares.

painted_upper_surfaces.colour: Off-white neutral to slightly warm; avoid stark emissive white and strong yellow.

dimensions_and_position_evidence_boundar: No exact tile size, grout width, floor slab module, dark band width, skirting height or wall-dado height is established by a ruler or dimensioned drawing.
No exact beam width/depth/spacing or ceiling height is established by these images.
No exact floor-band arrangement relative to the user's three doors, tuck shop, sink or two courtyards is established.
The user's whole-G-floor confirmation and current exterior model may constrain room extent; that does not convert photo estimates into measured dimensions.
Keep any provisional texture scale or material numeric settings identified as visual approximation.

bounded_search_outcome: Searches for ATS dining/floor/boarding photos did not reveal a newer labelled full-room material survey. General image search returned unrelated schools and was excluded. The inspected 2021 dry activity photo gives useful independent surface corroboration; nearby collage/art-room images in the same PDF were inspected and excluded as different rooms. No new original asset download was needed because the full-resolution source images were already present.
